Citation: Wiejak-Roy & Edwards, "Trends and challenges in regulation and accreditation of land surveying professions in the United States of America and the United Kingdom," Survey Review (Taylor & Francis), DOI: 10.1080/00396265.2025.2552025
Data_Used: Review of legal regulations and professional guidelines in US and UK
Key_Finding: Compares US and UK professional requirements for licensed land surveyors; highlights growing need for paraprofessionals (e.g. CST from NSPS) and challenges in encouraging new candidates
Gap_Limitation: Focused on regulation/accreditation rather than workforce demographics; no quantitative workforce data

Citation: Anonymous (Academia.edu), "Surveying Shortage: A Brief Look at the Evidence," unpublished/working paper, Academia.edu
Key_Finding: Analyzed evidence of the surveying shortage including age profile of profession and closing of university programs; found decades-long decline in entrants and increase in exits
Gap_Limitation: Not peer-reviewed; limited citation information available; author and date unclear

Citation: Heydari, Shojaei, Naderi & Iorio, "Paving the Way for Progress: A Systematic Literature Review on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion in the AEC Industry," Journal of Management in Engineering, 40(3)
Key_Finding: Identified 10 influential variable clusters affecting DEI in AEC industry including organizational aspects, work environment, work-life balance, education, and wage gap; mapped barriers and solutions
Gap_Limitation: Covers AEC broadly -- surveying is not specifically addressed as a subfield; focuses on published literature which may miss trade/gray literature

Citation: Choi, Shane & Chih (eds.), "Diversity and Inclusion in the Engineering-Construction Industry," Special Collection, Journal of Management in Engineering, 38(2)
Key_Finding: 23 articles exploring segregation, inequality, labor shortage, and discrimination in construction; concluded that increasing diversity is imperative for future workforce; more rigorous research needed
Gap_Limitation: Construction-focused; does not specifically address land surveying as distinct from broader AEC

Citation: Menches & Abraham, "Women in Construction -- Tipping the Balance," & related papers in JME special collection on retention of women in civil engineering workforce
Data_Used: Survey data on women in civil engineering
Key_Finding: Female civil engineers are underrepresented in supervisory positions, much more likely to leave their jobs, and experience more career path challenges; women earn 50.6% of environmental engineering degrees but only 25.9% of civil engineering degrees
Gap_Limitation: Limited to gender; does not address intersectionality with race; no surveying-specific data

Citation: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, "Occupational Outlook Handbook: Surveyors," 2024-2034 projections
Key_Finding: Employment of surveyors projected to grow 4% (2024-2034); about 3,900 annual openings mostly from replacement needs (retirements/exits); median wage $72,740; technology may limit growth
Gap_Limitation: BLS projects modest growth but does not model retirement wave separately; does not break out licensed vs. unlicensed surveyors

Citation: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, "Occupational Outlook Handbook: Surveying and Mapping Technicians," 2024-2034 projections
Key_Finding: Employment projected to grow 5% (2024-2034); about 7,600 annual openings; technicians still needed to interpret output of drones and new technologies
Gap_Limitation: Does not address demographics or diversity of the technician workforce

Citation: NSPS, "Surveying Profession Demographics Survey," National Society of Professional Surveyors
Key_Finding: Profession is 94.3% male, 92.3% White; Black representation at 0.3% (8 of 2409); Hispanic at 1.7%; largest income brackets $80-100K and $100K+
Gap_Limitation: Self-selected sample of NSPS members; may not represent non-members or unlicensed workforce; date of survey unclear

Citation: Data USA / U.S. Census ACS, "Surveyors, Cartographers & Photogrammetrists" demographic profile
Key_Finding: Workforce is 82.8% male, 83.1% White, 3.55% Black, 11.1% Hispanic; total workforce ~35,072
Gap_Limitation: Combines surveyors with cartographers and photogrammetrists; cannot isolate licensed land surveyors specifically

Citation: Zippia, "Land Surveyor Demographics and Statistics," labor market analysis
Key_Finding: 75.4% White, 10.9% Hispanic, 5.0% Asian, 3.35% Black; 93.9% male; diversity score 5.5/10; women earned 96% of male wages
Gap_Limitation: Methodology for data aggregation not fully transparent; mixes data sources

Citation: NCEES, "Squared 2024" Annual Report
Key_Finding: PS exam pass rate: 56% first-time, 39% repeat; FS exam historically ~46% first-time pass rate with only ~287 first-time takers (2016 data); low candidate volume (hundreds not thousands)
Gap_Limitation: Does not publish candidate demographics; historical trend data on candidate volume decline is scattered across annual reports

Citation: Gonzales & Keane, American Geosciences Institute, "Geoscience Workforce Projections 2019-2029"
Data_Used: BLS data and AGI workforce surveys
Key_Finding: Predicted 27% loss of existing geoscience workforce by 2029 due to retirements; supply of ~1,500 graduate degree recipients/year does not meet demand
Gap_Limitation: Covers geosciences broadly (geologists, hydrologists, etc.) -- not specific to surveying/geomatics; may overestimate losses if retirement is delayed

Citation: Bezdek, "Who Will Fill the Geoscience Workforce Supply Gap?" Environmental Science & Technology (ACS)
Key_Finding: Estimated shortfall of over 150,000 geoscientists in US over a decade; majority of geoscientists within 15 years of retirement
Gap_Limitation: Older projection (2009); actual shortfall may differ due to technology changes and economic cycles

Citation: Project Geospatial, "The GeoAI Revolution: Charting the 2030 Geospatial Workforce Landscape"
Data_Used: Industry analysis and AI adoption data
Key_Finding: 41% of employers plan workforce cuts due to AI by 2030; acute gap in mid-career registered professionals near retirement; skills mismatch between traditional geospatial and AI-centric roles
Gap_Limitation: Forward-looking projections with inherent uncertainty; does not isolate land surveying from broader geospatial

Citation: ASCE, "Diversity and Inclusion in Civil and Environmental Engineering," Special Issue, Journal of Professional Issues in Engineering Education and Practice, 144(4)
Journal_Source: J. Prof. Issues in Eng. Educ. and Practice (ASCE)
Key_Finding: Less than 15% of civil engineers are women and less than 20% are nonwhite; researchers historically focused on gender/race with absence of research on disability and socioeconomic status
Gap_Limitation: Noted absence of research on disability, veterans, socioeconomic status in civil engineering DEI literature

Citation: Wynn & Correll (and related JME papers), Gender Diversity in US Construction Industry Leaders, JME 36(5)
Key_Finding: Women fill only 3.9% of executive engineering billets despite earning 21.9% of civil engineering bachelor's degrees over 24 years
Gap_Limitation: Focused on leadership/executive level; does not address entry-level pipeline or retention at junior levels

Citation: Associated General Contractors of America / NCCER, "2025 Workforce Survey"
Key_Finding: 92% of firms report difficulty finding workers; 41% of construction workforce will retire by 2031; only 3% of young adults express interest in construction trades
Gap_Limitation: Industry-wide; does not break out surveying-specific subcontractor workforce

Citation: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies, "Rebuilding the Construction Trades Workforce"
Key_Finding: Construction lost ~1 million workers in Great Recession and has not recovered; 88% White and 89% male; minorities now 37% of workers (up from 27% in 2003) and women 11% (up from 9%)
Gap_Limitation: Broad construction workforce; includes laborers and operators who differ substantially from surveying professionals

Citation: McKinsey & Company, "Solving US Construction's Worker Shortage"
Key_Finding: Identified labor mismatch as core issue; recommended partnerships with nontraditional talent sources including veterans, formerly incarcerated, and underserved communities
Gap_Limitation: Consulting perspective; not peer-reviewed; may overstate tractability of solutions

Citation: Gitnux / WifiTalents, "Diversity Equity and Inclusion in the Plumbing Industry Statistics"
Key_Finding: Women are 2.1% of plumbers/pipefitters; 97.4% of contractors are male; Hispanic/Latino workers are 28.4% of plumbing workforce; 80% of tradeswomen report workplace harassment
Gap_Limitation: Aggregated statistics without primary methodology; may mix data years

Citation: UA (United Association), 2023 Diversity Pipeline Program data; PHCC Equity Hiring Toolkit adoption (2022)
Key_Finding: UA trained 1,200 underrepresented youth for plumbing apprenticeships; 75 contractors adopted PHCC toolkit increasing minority hires by 18%; DEI-curriculum apprenticeships saw 20% higher minority graduation
Gap_Limitation: Limited to participating organizations; selection effects likely; long-term retention data not reported

Citation: U.S. DOL, Apprenticeship data; SharkBite pre-apprenticeship analysis
Key_Finding: Women are 9% of active apprentices (2020); electrical sector saw 366% growth in young women apprentices over 5 years but overall female share remains under 5%; pre-apprenticeships targeting underrepresented populations show promise
Gap_Limitation: Electrical and plumbing data; no surveying apprenticeship comparison data exists

Citation: Esri, "Bridging the Gap: The Rising Demand for Geospatial Professionals Amid Declining Geography Majors"
Data_Used: Industry demand data and enrollment trends
Key_Finding: Exponential growth of digital geographic information generating continued demand for geospatial professionals at all levels; geography major enrollments declining while industry demand increases
Gap_Limitation: Blog post not peer-reviewed; does not provide demographic breakdown of GIS workforce

Citation: GIM International, "GIS Jobs: Too Many or Not Enough?"
Key_Finding: Skills mismatch: recent graduates report competition for GIS jobs while employers say they cannot attract right candidates; geospatial market ~$90B growing to $263B
Gap_Limitation: Does not address demographic composition of GIS workforce; focused on skills rather than diversity

Citation: NCARB, "NCARB by the Numbers" (2024 edition)
Key_Finding: 1 in 3 new architects is a person of color; 2 in 5 are women; 34% of new architects identified as person of color in 2023 (up from 25% in 2019); Black architects remain ~2% of practitioner population
Gap_Limitation: Architecture licensure data is far more granular than surveying licensure data; cannot directly compare to PLS demographics

Citation: AIA, "Diversity in the Profession of Architecture"
Data_Used: AIA member survey + Workplace Experiences Survey (1346 respondents)
Key_Finding: AIA membership is 67% White, 2% Black, 5% Hispanic, 6% Asian; white men have different workplace experience than all other groups; women of color report worst experiences
Gap_Limitation: Dated (2016); AIA membership may not represent full profession; self-reported data

Citation: NCARB/NOMA Joint Survey on minority licensure experience
Key_Finding: Identified how minority professionals experience obstacles on path to licensure; long path (5-6 year education + internship + exams) disproportionately burdens minorities and underserved populations
Gap_Limitation: Results may not be fully published; specific findings from survey not widely available in search results

Citation: Royal Academy of Engineering, "Equality, Diversity, and Inclusivity in Engineering, 2013 to 2022: A Review"
Key_Finding: COVID-19 exacerbated existing structural inequalities in STEM; inclusion challenges in engineering organizations intrinsically linked to systemic inequality in wider society
Gap_Limitation: UK-focused; may not directly apply to US context; engineering broadly rather than surveying

Citation: Oregon State University Geomatics Program report; ABET accreditation listings
Key_Finding: OSU geomatics thriving with 3 tenured faculty, 3 teaching faculty, 20 grad students, 44 undergrad minors; but nationwide only ~26 ABET-accredited surveying/geomatics programs remain; several programs recently closed (Phoenix College, UConn)
Gap_Limitation: No comprehensive national tracking of surveying program enrollments over time; closures documented anecdotally rather than systematically

Citation: SAM Companies, "Combatting the Talent Shortage with Apprenticeship Programs"
Key_Finding: SAM offering DOL-certified Geomatics Technician apprenticeship: 2-year program with on-the-job training and Journeyman Surveyor Certification; structured as alternative to traditional 4-year degree path
Gap_Limitation: Single company case; no outcome data on retention or demographic composition of apprentices reported
